```plato
    // Where the ray strikes the triangle. Misses when the ray is parallel to the
    // triangle's plane, when the crossing point falls outside the triangle, or when
    // it lies behind the ray origin. The reported normal is the triangle's own,
    // flipped when the ray arrives from behind it, so it always opposes the ray.
    // Face is 0 on a hit and -1 on a miss: a lone triangle is its own face 0.
    Raycast(tri: Triangle3D, r: Ray3D): RayHit3D
    {
        var m = MollerTrumbore(r, tri);
        var inv = 1.0 / m.X;
        var u = m.Y * inv;
        var v = m.Z * inv;
        var t = m.W * inv;
        var inside = u >= 0.0 && v >= 0.0 && u + v <= 1.0;
        var n = tri.Normal;
        var facing = n.Vector.Dot(r.Direction.Vector) <= 0.0 ? n : Direction3D(n.Vector.Negative);
        return m.X == 0.0 || !inside || t < 0.0
            ? (false, 0.0, r.Origin, n, FaceIndex(-1), BarycentricCoordinate(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), UvCoordinate(0.0, 0.0))
            : (true, t, r.PointAt(t), facing, FaceIndex(0),
               BarycentricCoordinate(1.0 - u - v, u, v), UvCoordinate(u, v));
    }
```
